parts.note: surface reading: an animal belonging to someone called Douglas
setter's reading: Douglas is the capital of the Isle of Man, so this is a pet native to that island

explanation.walkthrough: Douglas looks like a man's name, but it is the capital town of the Isle of Man, whose famous breed of cat has no tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The tailless feline breed originates on the island whose capital is Douglas, so it is that town's characteristic domestic animal.

clue.text: Cleans up after many quick operations

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so it stands for many
ops is the short, quick form of operations

explanation.surface: Someone tidying the theatre after a day of rapid surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: To mop is to wipe a floor clean with a wet sponge on a handle, so the verb matches tidying.

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece sitting on another means the first is placed above, so ahead of, the second

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A duck spotted swimming on a river in England.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck looks like the bird, but it is cricket's word for a batsman scoring zero.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nile is the great African waterway flowing north through Egypt, an example of the class named.

indicators.note: placing something in another word puts it inside that word's letters
in a down entry, raising letters lifts them upwards so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: first part of chase, the hunt
the letters of it's, turned upwards
rest of chase, the hunt

explanation.surface: A whip held up during a fox hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: CHASE (hunting) holds STI, which is IT'S read upwards: CHA-STI-SE.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise is to punish, originally physically, so it fits whip as a verb of beating or rebuking.

clue.text: Hothead in Chinese secret society gets the lash

indicators.note: something placed in another word sits inside its letters

parts.note: first letter of tong, a Chinese secret society
the head of hot is its opening letter
rest of tong

explanation.surface: A hot-tempered gang member in a Chinese society is flogged.
explanation.walkthrough: A tong is a Chinese secret society, especially in American Chinatowns; H goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is a strip of leather, and as a whip's lash it is the striking part, a direct synonym.

parts.note: Chas is a short form of Charles
Ed is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: Someone being run after by a pair of lads.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue prints Persued, a misspelling of pursued. The two boys are CHAS and ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be chased is to have someone running after you, the same sense as being pursued.

clue.text: It secures a superior item for ladies

definitions.text: It secures a superior item for ladies

parts.note: surface reading: some high-quality product sold for women
setter's reading: superior means placed above, so the item worn on top of the head, kept in place

explanation.walkthrough: Superior suggests excellence, but here it means literally on top: the thing on a woman's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A long pin pushed through a woman's headwear and hair holds that headwear firmly in place.

parts.note: surface reading: drinking too much before bed
setter's reading: after excess drink you go to bed drunk, and tight is slang for drunk, turning the bedtime wish into a literal instruction

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the bedtime farewell, read literally: go to bed while tipsy, since tight means drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a goodnight wish, but its second word is slang for intoxicated, so it describes slumbering after excess drink.

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside its letters

parts.note: start of demise, a death
oral means spoken aloud
rest of demise

explanation.surface: Words spoken through a dying person's last gasp.
explanation.walkthrough: Death rattle looks like one phrase, but the definition is rattle alone. ORAL goes inside DEMISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle someone is to unnerve them, and to demoralise is to sap their confidence, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Switch the spot dance as part of a pattern

indicators.note: to switch two things is to swap their places, so the two clued words are joined in the opposite order

parts.note: the polka is a lively Bohemian dance
a dot is a spot

explanation.surface: Changing the place where a dance is held, as part of some planned routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A polka dot is one of the round spots repeated over fabric, so it is a single element of a design.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a flow of water or air
second meaning: a continuous line of people moving along, as in walking in single file

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the latest computer document; neither word has that sense here.
explanation.definitionFit: A brook or flow of water is a current, and people pouring out in a line stream out, as a file does.

parts.note: surface reading: something is inexpensive by American standards
setter's reading: an American adjective meaning cheap or trifling, taken from an old coin worth a quarter dollar

explanation.walkthrough: A bit was a unit of 12.5 cents in old America, so two of them made a quarter; the word came to mean worthless or tawdry.
explanation.definitionFit: In US slang the term describes something trivial, petty or shoddy, from the small quarter-dollar coin value.

parts.note: surface reading: the street and number of a home
setter's reading: the house is a theatre audience, and an address to it is an actor's aside meant to be heard by all

explanation.walkthrough: House means the audience in a theatre, and address means speech, not a postal location.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's loud aside, supposedly unheard by other characters but meant for the audience, is a speech aimed at the theatre.

parts.note: stocks are shares in companies
to till is to plough and cultivate land

explanation.surface: Investments left untouched, while one tends the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock-still means completely motionless, as rigid as a post, which is what unmoving describes.

clue.text: Remember to ring for a baby-sitter?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, whimsical: to phone someone to watch over, or mind, the child

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: phone someone to look after the kids.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to recall or bring something back into one's thoughts, a direct synonym of the first word.

clue.text: Rent as new, holding key as duplicate

indicators.note: one part holding another keeps it inside, wrapped around it
making something new remakes it, so these letters are reshaped into a fresh order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
a crib is a key, a literal translation used by students to cheat

explanation.surface: A landlord re-lets a flat as new, keeping a key as a copy.
explanation.walkthrough: Key here is a crib or translation aid, not something for a lock.
explanation.definitionFit: To transcribe is to write out a copy of text, so it means to duplicate in writing.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to tear away, read as a phrasal verb
second meaning: a swindle or fraud

explanation.walkthrough: Tearaway suggests a reckless youth, but it is read as tear away, a phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rip something off is to tear it away, and as a noun the term means a swindle or overcharge.

indicators.note: coming after means the first named piece is written after the second one

parts.note: fifty less one, written in the informal Roman way
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about counting, with a denial.
explanation.walkthrough: IL for forty-nine is not proper Roman numerals (XLIX is), which may be the joke in the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sick is the opposite of being healthy, so the answer means not in good health.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a central upright beam in a roof truss
second meaning, whimsical: letters belonging to a monarch

explanation.walkthrough: Royal Mail is the British postal service; here it is read as a monarch's correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: In carpentry the vertical timber rising from tie-beam to ridge in a roof truss is a structural brace.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a low point in a mountain ridge
second meaning: the standard abbreviation for colonel

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a permit for an officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A col is the lowest saddle between mountain peaks, and it is also the abbreviated military rank of colonel.

clue.text: They reveal the stars in all their splendour

definitions.text: They reveal the stars in all their splendour

parts.words: They reveal the stars in all their splendour
parts.note: surface reading: telescopes or clear skies showing the night sky
setter's reading: stars are performers on stage, lit up by powerful theatre lamps

explanation.walkthrough: Stars suggests astronomy, but they are stage performers picked out by theatre lamps.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre lamps throw a narrow, intense beam onto a lead performer so the audience sees them clearly.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a walkout where all the workers go out
second meaning: to deliver a blow

explanation.walkthrough: All-out hit reads as a full-force blow, but all-out is the first definition: every worker out.
explanation.definitionFit: Industrial action where the whole workforce leaves is the noun sense, and to deliver a blow is the verb.

clue.text: Horse-racing is the thing for Cambridge college

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the traditional nickname for the turf
second meaning, whimsical: an activity belonging to King's, a Cambridge college

explanation.walkthrough: King's College is one of the University of Cambridge's colleges, and sport means the pastime that belongs to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Racing thoroughbreds has long been nicknamed after monarchs' patronage of it, the pastime traditionally favoured by royalty.

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter, so being topless means losing it

parts.note: Sicily is the large island off the toe of Italy

explanation.surface: Bare-breasted sunbathing on a Mediterranean beach gets a cold stare.
explanation.walkthrough: SICILY loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Icily means in a cold, unfriendly manner, which is exactly what frostily means as an adverb.

clue.text: Tongue of land joining Cambodia and Myanmar

definitions.text: Tongue of land joining Cambodia and Myanmar

parts.note: surface reading: a narrow spit or isthmus of territory
setter's reading: a tongue is a language, that of the country lying between Cambodia and Myanmar

explanation.walkthrough: Tongue of land looks like geography, but tongue means language, the one spoken in the country between those two.
explanation.definitionFit: The official language of Thailand, which borders both Cambodia and Myanmar, is spoken by most of its people.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to arise or originate from, as a verb
second meaning: the stalk that holds up a bloom

explanation.walkthrough: Spring suggests the season of blooms, but it is the verb meaning to originate.
explanation.definitionFit: To stem from something is to originate in it, and a plant's stalk bears its blossoms.

indicators.note: to catch something is to grab and hold it, so one word holds the other inside

parts.note: start of Iris, a girl's name
taken as written
end of Iris

explanation.surface: A girl comes down with an eye infection.
explanation.walkthrough: IRIS, also part of the eye, holds IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Iritis is inflammation of the coloured ring around the pupil, a medical condition of the eye.

clue.text: How one bounces back after being fired

definitions.text: How one bounces back after being fired

parts.words: How one bounces back after being fired
parts.note: surface reading: recovering after losing one's job
setter's reading: one is a bullet shot from a gun, which rebounds off a hard surface

explanation.walkthrough: Fired suggests dismissal from work; here it is shooting a projectile.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebound of a bullet or stone off a surface at an angle is the deflection described.

clue.text: Defect in the hose used by firemen

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a run in stockings or tights
second meaning: climbing equipment carried on fire engines

explanation.walkthrough: Hose and firemen suggest a fire hose, but hose here means stockings; a ladder is the British word for a run in them.
explanation.definitionFit: A vertical run in tights is called this in Britain, and the climbing frame of rungs is standard fire equipment.

clue.text: Showing unusual maturity, but lacking a certain element

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary, so these letters are put out of their normal order
lacking something means going without it, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
the letter to be removed

explanation.surface: A precocious person who is nonetheless missing some vital quality.
explanation.walkthrough: MATURITY without its A is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Yttrium is a silvery metallic chemical element, number 39, named after the Swedish village Ytterby.
